acceptanceCriteria: store.Mutate (notes, ticket writes, evidence, obligation witness), attempt heartbeat, release and every read verb resume from a verified checkpoint and validate only receipts after it, with the same refusals as a full audit for any prefix tampering the checkpoint binds (spec requirement + negative tests).
The checkpoint is refreshed under the existing writer lock by whoever extends it; concurrent processes share it instead of each redoing the prefix.
A retained measurement on a >=47k-receipt store with the head moving every 30 s: note write and heartbeat < 1 s, read < 0.5 s, CPU scales with receipts since the checkpoint, not total length.
--timing (or the existing audit-mode output) reports FULL vs CHECKPOINT_PLUS_TAIL on mutation verbs.
Full-audit fallback when the checkpoint is absent, stale, or fails its binding is retained and tested.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1072 (2026-10-17, owner-prioritised). On a ~47,700-receipt (455 MB) store, `ticket note set` takes 47 s wall / 45 s user, CPU-bound in cli.noteCommand -> submitMutation -> store.Mutate -> mutateLocked -> journal.Reader.auditForMutation -> audit -> walk (Reader.step/validateRecord, wire parser, checkHostile, snapshot.ReceiptRestorer.Next restoring elided receipts). Reads after any head move pay the same walk (ticket show >51 s, queue status 14 s vs 0.1-0.2 s at an unmoved head). Five live attempts' heartbeats ran 0:38-2:21 each at 65-125% CPU; total ~640% CPU in corvint-tasks. The read path already has a retained checkpoint (journal.Checkpoint, CHECKPOINT_PLUS_TAIL in cli/lease.go readCheckpoint) and lease writes have verified-cache reuse, but auditForMutation calls audit(nil, requestID, lim, false) with no checkpoint. Broader than #1063 (V1-1626, pool acquire). Related: #1055 (V1-1618 journal retention), #1010, V1-1617/#1069.
title: Tasks store: every store.Mutate write and checkpoint-missing read re-audits the whole journal from receipt 1 (45 s CPU per note write at 47k receipts) (issue #1072)
